title: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair
snippet: Dense 3D tracking from monocular video requires establishing point correspondences over time, estimating their depth, and inferring their trajectories during occlusion. Existing methods typically learn these tasks jointly, a demanding objective given the scarcity of 4D supervision. We show that strong pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models provide an effective foundation: lifted trajectories, with occluded segments simply interpolated, already rival dedicated 3D trackers using the same geometry. summary: ReLift is a paper on dense 3D tracking from monocular video. It lifts trajectories from pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models, then repairs the errors, especially under occlusion, instead of learning everything jointly.
whyItMatters: It shows that composing strong pretrained models can rival dedicated 3D trackers despite scarce 4D supervision.

title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
snippet: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression. LoCo detects candidate overthinking states from the model's own traces, freezes the corresponding reason…
summary: LoCo is a local preference learning method that compresses reasoning by detecting overthinking states in a model's own traces and teaching it to stop once it has enough information.

title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
snippet: Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. Existing MCP environment-scaling methods are data-centric: they first synthesize a database and scenario, then derive tools and tasks from them. As a result, tool interfaces may not match real ones, tool compositions are not grounded in execution, and tasks rarely span more than one environment. We propose ToolSpace, a tool-centric framework that reverses this order. ToolSpace mines data, state, and retry dependencies from adjacent calls in execution traces of re…
summary: ToolSpace synthesizes agent training environments tool-first, mining dependencies from real MCP execution traces so tool interfaces and cross-environment tasks are grounded.

This is because lessons are inferred from trajectories labeled only with task success or failure, yet are typically provided without the trajectories they came from, leaving the agent no way to check them. title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
snippet: Low-bit quantization reduces the inference cost of LLM agents but can compromise task success. Examining failed rollouts, we find that quantized agents overlook task requirements or environmental conditions, producing environment transitions that diverge from successful full-precision references. Correcting these behavioral divergences remains difficult: offline data may miss the student's failure contexts, while its own rollouts may provide few correct responses in those contexts. We introduce SteerDistill, a quantization-aware distillation method in which a full-precision teacher guides the…
summary: SteerDistill is a quantization-aware distillation method where a full-precision teacher steers a low-bit LLM agent in a closed loop. It targets quantized agents that overlook task requirements or environment conditions and drift from successful full-precision rollouts.
whyItMatters: Cheaper low-bit agents that keep task success would cut inference costs for agent deployments.

title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
snippet: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. title: VoxMel TTS Technical Report

title: Accelerating Mixture of Block Attention via Dynamic Routing, KV-Centric Execution and Runtime Pipelining
snippet: Mixture of Block Attention (MoBA) reduces long-context computation by selecting key-value (KV) blocks for each query. FlashMoBA implements MoBA efficiently but retains a fixed Top-k budget and query-centric schedule. Fixed Top-k applies one budget across different score distributions and couples routing to task granularity; query-range ownership fragments K/V reuse when several ranges select the same column. We present LightningMoBA, which co-designs selection and execution through dynamic routing, KV-centric ownership, and runtime pipelining. Dynamic routing thresholds MoBA's per-query block…
